instructions: If all and only all commands fail to execute, declare error with <|ERROR|>.
You have solved this issue when this goal is met: The status of all pods say 'RUNNING'.
After every step, check to see if you have met the goal.
If you believe you have met the goal, declare solved with <|SOLVED|>.
If steps do not solve or need info, declare <|FAILED|>.
Do not use live feed flags like kubectl logs -f.
Do not use commands like vim or vi.
Do not use commands that open editors like kubectl edit.
guidelines: If command succeeds with no output, that is expected.
If placeholder <pod_name> appears, run kubectl get first.
Do not use live feed flags like kubectl logs -f.
If you do not conclude on an answer or a code then try again please.
Do not use commands like vim or vi.
Do not use commands that open editors like kubectl edit.

knowledge-prompt.problem-desc: The pod on my Kubernetes cluster cannot be accessed by making a curl request. Any requests made to the application running in this pod result in a timeout.
knowledge-prompt.system-prompt: Give specific commands to fix this issue. If modifying file contents is necessary, use the sed command to achieve this. If providing a file path, make sure to keep the full file path. Suggest only the essential steps needed to solve the issue. Be frugal.

debug-prompt.additional-directions: If any deployment files are modified, reapply the deployment to the cluster.
